maria: heads-up: after the kernel-selector change yesterday I'm seeing a weird perf shift in KV-heavy workloads. p50 gen went from ~28ms -> ~48ms on our 8k token smoke test :grimacing:

maria: ran an nsys trace and attached the timeline (short excerpt below). main hotspot moved from matmul_fused -> kv_cache_lookup + batch_coalescer stalls. trace: /tmp/nsys_kv_shift.qdrep

maria: nsys cmd I ran:
```
nsys profile --sample=none --trace=nvtx,cuda --output=/tmp/nsys_kv_shift \
  --capture-range=cpu:profiler_start:profiler_end \
  --force-overwrite --capture-contexts=all \
  python perf_run.py --model=gpt-small --batch=16 --seq=8192
```

akshay: thanks. do you have the kernel timeline sample? interested if matmul fallback to cuBLAS happened or if our fused kernel was selected but slower.

maria: excerpted timeline:
```
00:00.000 - matmul_fused (old hot path) 18%
00:00.120 - kv_cache_lookup 32%
00:00.500 - batch_coalescer_idle 14%
00:01.000 - attention_kernel_v2 8%
00:01.200 - kv_cache_insert 6%
```

maria: looks like the selector started preferring a small-block matmul that increases synchronization between batch lanes, causing batch_coalescer to wait and KV lookups to dominate.

sven: rolling bisect suggestion: start between the runtime change that touched kernel_selector + the batching policy tweak PR. I can run git-bisect with a smoke harness.

julia: I repro locally with perf build. quick numbers: before (commit a1b2c3) p50=27.9ms, after (commit f9e8d7) p50=48.2ms. token throughput dropped ~28%.

perf-bot: bisect-run started by sven. harness: ./tools/smoke_bisect.sh --target=perf --repeats=3 --timeout=600

sven: preliminary bisect narrowed it to 3 commits. suspect culprits: 1) kernel-selector: fallback heuristics, 2) batch_coalescer: lock ordering change, 3) kv-cache: LRU threshold tweak.

akshay: can you paste the small nvprof summary? I'm curious about cudaMemset vs kernel time ratio.

maria: nvprof summary (after):
```
GPU activities:
  % time  Time(%)  Name
  32.1%   1.02s    kv_cache_lookup
  24.0%   0.76s    matmul_small_block
  14.3%   0.45s    batch_coalescer_kernel
   8.0%   0.25s    attention_kernel_v2
```

maria: before nvprof (baseline):
```
  46.0%   1.15s    matmul_fused
  18.0%   0.45s    kv_cache_lookup
  10.0%   0.25s    attention_kernel_v2
```

julia: interesting — matmul_fused used to hide KV costs by being dominant on the timeline. selector change split matmul into matmul_small_block which is less efficient and interleaves more with KV ops.

sven: bisect result: commit hash 7f4d2a9 toggled the selector to prefer heuristic X for small batch sizes. Reverting that line restores baseline latency on my rig.

akshay: do we know why selector picked heuristic X? input distribution changed? maybe seq distribution or mem-use estimate calc bug.

maria: I diffed the model input profile used by selector: the expected average kv-hit-rate dropped from 0.78 -> 0.65 because of a minor change in caching warmup timers, so selector thought smaller matmuls were cheaper.

julia: TL;DR: warmup timer tweak -> lower predicted KV hit-rate -> selector picks matmul_small_block -> more interleaving -> batch_coalescer stalls -> p50 increase.

maria: mitigation options: 1) revert warmup timer (quick), 2) update selector to account for KV hit-rate stdev and prefer stable fused matmul when variance high, 3) tune batch_coalescer to prefetch KV keys and reduce stalls.

sven: my vote: revert warmup timer in 7f4d2a9 for the patch release, then follow-up with selector change that uses a smoothed hit-rate. I'll open PR.

akshay: agree. also put a perf test into CI that runs a KV-stress trace and asserts matmul dominance > 40% on baseline config.

perf-bot: note added to perf-regressions board: issue #2482 created (kv-batcher-kernel-shift).

maria: thanks everyone. I'll attach the full qdrep and nvprof logs to the issue and link the bisect output. :thumbsup:
